items.current:
- BROKER qualifies EFFECT_GATE as a peer (artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start,
  SO_PEERCRED) before BIND_EXECUTION. EFFECT_GATE qualifies the broker the same way
  on every I05 frame and the writer on every I07 frame.
items.proposed:
- BROKER qualifies EFFECT_GATE as a peer (artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start, SO_PEERCRED) before BIND_EXECUTION.
  Its artifact check reads the gate's `/proc/<pid>/exe` link, which the kernel allows as long as the gate holds no
  capability (the signed I04 port is 1024 or above, Q-HE2S-9 (a)), stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)) and runs with uid
  and gid 0 like the broker (O-W03-PEER-EXE).
- A peer's start time is compared on every frame with a reference taken without a race at its first frame, through a
  pidfd that names the connected process itself (SO_PEERPIDFD, or SCM_PIDFD on a frame); a pidfd_open of the
  SO_PEERCRED pid alone does not give one, because that pid may already name a later process (HS43).
- EFFECT_GATE qualifies the broker on every I05 frame by label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED (HS43). It does
  not check the broker's artifact. Reading `/proc/<pid>/exe` is a ptrace-mode read (PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS);
  without CAP_SYS_PTRACE, which no role holds, the kernel allows it only if the target's permitted capabilities are a
  subset of the reader's effective ones, and the broker's (§5.3) are not a subset of the gate's, so the kernel
  refuses the gate that read. The broker's executable identity follows from its label instead: SELinux matrix v4
  (`architecture/selinux-matrix-v2/`) lets `planeon_broker_t` be entered only from init through
  `planeon_broker_exec_t`, which only a maintenance boot may relabel, and denies `execute_no_trans` on every type.
- EFFECT_GATE qualifies the writer on every I07 frame by artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED (HS43).
  For the artifact it opens the `/proc/<pid>` directory of the pidfd's process, with no window in which the PID could
  be reused, and reads its `exe` link with `readlinkat` on that directory descriptor (§5.3) into a buffer longer than
  the enrolled writer path (§4.2); the link must equal that path exactly, with no " (deleted)" suffix. The fs-verity
  digest is enforced on the sealed file the path names; the gate does not re-measure it per frame (opening the link
  and FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY are not in its allowlist). The kernel allows the read without CAP_SYS_PTRACE only while
  the gate's filesystem uid and gid equal the writer's real, effective and saved uids and gids (all 0), the writer is
  dumpable, and the writer's permitted capabilities are a subset of the gate's effective ones, which the writer's
  empty set (§5.3) always is; SELinux matrix v4 gives `planeon_gate_t` `file read` on `planeon_policy_writer_t`
  (`procAccess`), the LSM check of that read. Yama (ptrace_scope 3) limits only ptrace attach, not this read, and
  /proc must be mounted without a hidepid option that hides the peers. Obligation O-W03-WRITER-EXE holds both sides
  to this. Until the gate's filter admits `readlinkat` (O-SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT), the writer's artifact check is
  decided but open (Q-HE3A-1b) and the other four checks apply.
items.why: The gate cannot read the broker's exe link (commoncap: the target's permitted set must lie in the reader's effective set), so the broker is qualified without an artifact check and identified by its label (Q-HE2S-10, Q-HS43-1); the writer keeps the artifact check through its exe link (Q-HE3A-1 (c)) under the kernel's stated preconditions; the broker's check of the gate holds because the gate has no capability (Q-HE2S-9) and stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7); the start time is compared with a race-free reference, so pidfd/start closes the PID-reuse window (Q-HS43-1).

## 12. Amendment HS43 (2026-10-15)

HS43 changes how the effect gate qualifies its two local peers (§4.3) and states the one system call the writer's
executable check needs (§5.3); the gate's filter admits that call only once O-SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT lands. It is
applied to the W02D effective text, which stays byte-identical; `architecture/host-interface-amendment-hs43/amendment.json`
gives every change and its reason.

| Item | Where | Decisions |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | 4.3 | Q-HE2S-10, Q-HE2S-7, Q-HE2S-9, Q-HE3A-1, Q-HS43-1 |
| H2 | 5.3 EFFECT_GATE row, capabilities | Q-HE3A-1 |
| H3 | 5.3 EFFECT_GATE row, seccomp | Q-HE3A-1, Q-HE3A-1b, HS43-START |
| H4 | 7 | Q-HE2S-10 |

The data follow in order (Q-HE3A-1b): the W02d v3 allowlist (`architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v3/`) gains the
EFFECT_GATE `readlinkat` rule in its own packet, then the EFFECT_GATE programs and the edge record are republished,
then R10 re-vendors them and adds the check.

Obligations: O-SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT (the allowlist rule), O-W03-WRITER-EXE (the writer's credentials and dumpability, and the read bound to the frame's process), O-W03-PEER-EXE (the gate readable by the broker, and race-free peer pidfds), O-T04-HS43 (native confirmation). Every E01-E12 obligation stays OPEN_UNPROVEN.
items.why: Section 12 lists the items, the superseded clauses, the residuals, the order of the data packets and the obligations.

dispositions.summary: The gate qualifies the broker by label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED; its executable identity follows from its label; the BIND digest is the mutual record with the narrower gate-side half.
The gate stays dumpable, so the broker can read its exe link.
The gate holds no capability, so its permitted set lies inside the broker's.
The gate checks the writer's executable through its exe link, under the kernel's ptrace-read rules.
The specification states the readlinkat duty; the allowlist rule follows in its own packet.
The duty admits readlinkat only with a dirfd other than AT_FDCWD (a non-negative int).
Only the artifact is dropped; pidfd/start stays, compared with a race-free reference.

obligations.label: the allowlist rule
obligations.owner: the parallel lane's next harness-onion packet (the W02d v3 allowlist amendment, Q-HE3A-1b)
obligations.text: Add to the EFFECT_GATE row of architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v3/ a readlinkat rule for x86_64 and aarch64 that admits only a non-negative dirfd judged on the low 32 bits of argument 0, which refuses AT_FDCWD (0xffffff9c) whatever the upper bits and any other negative value; one masked condition, (arg0 & 0x80000000) == 0, expresses it in the v3 model. Keep readlink unlisted, change no other role, and republish the vectors with AT_FDCWD in both encodings (0xffffffffffffff9c and 0x00000000ffffff9c) and -1 as killed cases.

obligations.label: the writer's credentials and dumpability, and the read bound to the frame's process
obligations.owner: W03 (the writer and the gate's I07 check; HE-007 per owner decision Q-HE3A-1b)
obligations.text: Run the writer with real, effective and saved uid and gid 0 and an empty permitted capability set, and keep it dumpable: no PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0, and an exec that changes no credentials (an artifact with no set-id bit and no file capabilities, started with equal uids and gids, and readable by the starting domain, planeon_admin_t, which matrix v4 gives READ on planeon_policy_writer_exec_t). Run the gate with filesystem uid and gid 0. Take the writer's pidfd from the socket (SO_PEERPIDFD or SCM_PIDFD), open /proc/<pid> for that process with no PID-reuse window, read the exe link into a buffer longer than the enrolled path, and accept it only if it equals that path exactly.

obligations.label: the gate readable by the broker, and race-free peer pidfds
obligations.text: Keep the gate dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)), with uid and gid 0 and no capability after its seal (Q-HE2S-9 (a)), so the broker's read of its exe link passes the kernel's ptrace-read rules; take every peer pidfd from the socket (SO_PEERPIDFD at accept or SCM_PIDFD on a frame) or otherwise race-free, so a pidfd_open of a SO_PEERCRED pid is never the only reference, and read each peer's start time once through that pidfd's process.

obligations.label: native confirmation
obligations.text: On the enrolled kernel, confirm: the gate's readlinkat of the writer's exe link succeeds under the gate's filter and the writer's credentials; the same read of the broker's exe link fails with EACCES (an audited `capability sys_ptrace` denial for planeon_gate_t is expected, not a breach); the broker can read the gate's exe link; on x86_64 readlink kills the gate, and on both architectures readlinkat with AT_FDCWD in either encoding, or with -1, kills it; and the exact-path comparison refuses a longer path and a " (deleted)" target.
